chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mu'tamir (one performing Tamattu' Hajj) when he shaves his head before visiting the House (Kaaba), whether he applies henna to it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the henna, and the clothes, and the perfume, and everything except for the women.' He repeated it to me twice or three times. I said: 'And I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the henna, and the clothes, and the perfume, and everything except for the women.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يَطْلِيهِ: He applies it (referring to applying henna)

ai.seo_question: What is permissible for a Mu'tamir after shaving his head before visiting the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the prohibition on sexual intercourse remains the sole restriction for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who performs the initial shaving (Qasr) before the Tawaf al-Ziyarah, distinguishing this stage from the final state of Ihram. The repetition of the ruling by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and the confirmation by Imam al-Rida (AS) underscore the consensus on the permissibility of henna, clothing, and perfume during this intermediate phase. This ruling highlights the gradual transition of rituals in the Tamattu' Hajj, where most Ihram restrictions are lifted after the first Tawaf but before the final Sa'i.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Saeed Bin Yasaar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the performer of Tumatto when he shaves off his head before he visits the House (Kabah), whether he can apply henna upon it’. Heasws said: ‘Yes, the henna, and the clothes, and the perfume, and everything except for the women’. Heasws re-iterated it upon me twice or thrice’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about it, so heasws said: ‘Yes, the henna, and the (normal) clothes, and the perfume, and everything except for the women’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Sa‘id ibn Yasar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) after shaving, before visiting the House: if he can apply dyes. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, dyes, clothes, perfumes and everything becomes permissible except women.’ He (the Imam) repeated it twice or three times. I asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it and he (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, dyes, clothes, perfumes and everything becomes permissible except women.’”
